risks.risk: Dependence on MoD project execution and defence outlays
risks.note: Delays by the MoD in executing AD&S projects, shortfalls in planned defence outlays or adverse changes to government policy directly impact the Company's activities and consequently its revenues.

risks.risk: Uneven and skewed sales pattern driven by government decision-making
risks.note: Because projects are initiated by the MoD on its own policies and priorities, whether they progress into long-term programmes with a definitive quantum of orders depends largely on government decisions — producing a lumpy revenue profile beyond the Company's control.
Any material reallocation of the government's spending priorities could have a knock-on effect on the Company's activities and revenues.

risks.risk: Long approval and certification cycles in A&D
risks.note: Products and systems involve complex advanced technologies, so approval and certification cycles often extend materially longer than planned, delaying production orders and deliveries and shifting the timing of revenues.

risks.risk: Foreign currency and interest rate risk from rising international exposure
risks.note: The Company's increasing exposure to international markets brings inherent Foreign Currency Risk and Interest Rate risk.

Threats to the domestic A&D industry are largely policy-rooted — fiscal slippages, lengthy procurement and evaluation processes, corruption controversies and disputes over shortlisting in competitive bids — which delay acquisition plans and the execution timing of already long-dated projects; a large share of capital allocations is also pre-committed to existing obligations, leaving little room for new procurement.

risks.risk: Execution uncertainty around DAP 2026 and the phasing-down of offsets
risks.note: The draft DAP 2026's impact depends on execution — routes such as Strategic Partnership and 'Make-I' have historically seen limited maturation — while the de-emphasis of offsets removes an avenue previously available to domestic industry.

risks.risk: External macro, geopolitical and supply-chain risks
risks.note: A prolonged slowdown in India and/or the global economy, change or delay in domestic economic reforms, political instability, hostilities, and disruptions to global supply chains and cross-border trade (including tariff and export-control measures) are flagged as external risk factors.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SIKA is actively involved in four main areas: engineering (design and development); manufacturing, assembly and testing; projects and systems integration; and maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), with in-house technology development and production capabilities complemented by tie-ups with international partners. Building on established expertise in systems integration, documentation and certification, the Company works on a number of prestigious Indian projects within the Aerospace, Defence & Space sector, offering customers a combination of one or more of design, development, manufacturing, assembly, testing, certification, supply and integration of systems, and implementation of the projects under typically long-gestation programmes. It has also set up facilities to provide MRO for its own products and, with the backing of its customers, with foreign partners to provide MRO services for their AD&S products in India.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Continued increase in domestic defence spending: GoI defence allocation for FY 2026-27 raised to a record Rs 7.85 lakh crore (~USD 82.6 billion), up about 15.2% over FY 2025-26 Budget Estimates
- Reservation of a large share of the capital procurement budget for Indian industry — about Rs 1.39 lakh crore for FY 2026-27, plus 25% of the defence R&D budget for private industry, start-ups and academia
- Heightened demand signals following Operation Sindoor, including emergency procurements and near-full (99.6%) utilisation of the FY 2025-26 defence budget
- Aircraft and Aero Engines segment allocated Rs 63,734 crore (~USD 6.7 billion) for FY 2026-27, a ~31% increase reflecting priority on air power and standoff capability
- MoD modernisation drive expected to result in capital expenditure of about USD 250 billion over the next 10 years across fighter aircraft, radars, missiles, warships and allied systems
- Policy reforms lowering entry barriers and easing teaming between foreign OEMs and Indian entities — DAP 2020, draft DAP 2026, positive indigenisation lists, iDEX, SPV route
- Record domestic defence production of Rs 1.54 lakh crore in FY 2024-25 with a Government target of Rs 3 lakh crore of production by 2029
- Higher indigenous R&D funding: defence R&D capital outlay raised to Rs 17,250 crore (~USD 1.8 billion) and DRDO allocation to Rs 29,100 crore
- Offsets being de-emphasised in favour of direct indigenisation, co-development and indigenous content under draft DAP 2026
- Threats to timing: lengthy procurement and evaluation processes, committed-liability-heavy capital budgets, and long approval/certification cycles that delay production orders and deliveries

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Position the Company to capture India's defence indigenisation push, where roughly 75% of the modernisation (capital acquisition) budget is earmarked for domestic industry
- Make balancing investments in expanding the Company's operating base to support sustained and consistent growth over the medium term
- Participate in the opening up of the defence sector to private participation and in policy routes favouring 'Buy (Indian-IDDM)', indigenous design and IP ownership
- Dividend is recommended by the Board on the basis of the Company's performance and is subject to members' approval at the AGM; for the year under review the Directors recommended a dividend on equity shares payable to members on the record date. No amount is proposed to be transferred to the general reserve for the year. The Company has four wholly owned subsidiaries and no associate companies or joint ventures as on 31st March 2026. The Company does not have a stock option plan, so no director holds stock options; Executive Directors receive a performance incentive linked to the Company's profitability and each Independent Director receives a performance incentive of 0.50% of net profit, with non-executive directors otherwise paid only sitting fees. Directors state the accounts are prepared on a going concern basis with adequate internal financial controls, and there were no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position between the year-end and the date of the report.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report contains no rupee capex plan, named project, capacity number or commissioning timeline. Expansion is described only qualitatively: in recent years the Company has been focused on building advanced facilities to expand its operational base, to keep pace with the fast-paced development of the AD&S sector in India, leaving it positioned to meet the requirements of both potential international partners and domestic projects. Separately, the Company has set up facilities to provide MRO for its own products and, with the backing of its customers, has set up facilities with foreign partners to provide MRO services for their AD&S products in India. The Board's Report states there was no change in the nature of business during the year, no material change in the nature of the business of the four wholly owned subsidiaries, and no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position between the end of the financial year and the date of the report.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of the select private enterprises to have held CEMILAC design approvals continuously from 1999 through 2020 — a durable certification/approval barrier in AD&S
- Holds an Industrial License for Defence production from the Government of India, which enables it to undertake defence projects, plus DGAQA approval and AS9100 certification
- Established expertise in systems integration, documentation and certification across long-gestation AD&S programmes, allowing it to bundle design, development, manufacturing, testing, certification, supply and integration
- In-house technology development and production capabilities complemented by tie-ups with international partners
- MRO facilities for its own products and, with customer backing, with foreign partners for their AD&S products in India — an aftermarket/annuity layer
- Professional and experienced multi-background team focused on product quality and strong after-sales support
- External recognition: Financial Times 'High-Growth Companies Asia-Pacific' 2026 (fourth time in the last nine years), TIME 'India's Fastest Growing Companies' 2026, and 'Listed SME of the Year' at the Economic Times MSME Awards 2025

- Uneven and skewed sales pattern driven by government decision-making — Because projects are initiated by the MoD on its own policies and priorities, whether they progress into long-term programmes with a definitive quantum of orders depends largely on government decisions — producing a lumpy revenue profile beyond the Company's control.
- Rejig of government spending priorities — Any material reallocation of the government's spending priorities could have a knock-on effect on the Company's activities and revenues.
- Long approval and certification cycles in A&D — Products and systems involve complex advanced technologies, so approval and certification cycles often extend materially longer than planned, delaying production orders and deliveries and shifting the timing of revenues.
- Foreign currency and interest rate risk from rising international exposure — The Company's increasing exposure to international markets brings inherent Foreign Currency Risk and Interest Rate risk.
- Sector-level procurement and policy frictions — Threats to the domestic A&D industry are largely policy-rooted — fiscal slippages, lengthy procurement and evaluation processes, corruption controversies and disputes over shortlisting in competitive bids — which delay acquisition plans and the execution timing of already long-dated projects; a large share of capital allocations is also pre-committed to existing obligations, leaving little room for new procurement.
- Execution uncertainty around DAP 2026 and the phasing-down of offsets — The draft DAP 2026's impact depends on execution — routes such as Strategic Partnership and 'Make-I' have historically seen limited maturation — while the de-emphasis of offsets removes an avenue previously available to domestic industry.
- External macro, geopolitical and supply-chain risks — A prolonged slowdown in India and/or the global economy, change or delay in domestic economic reforms, political instability, hostilities, and disruptions to global supply chains and cross-border trade (including tariff and export-control measures) are flagged as external risk factors.
